newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec S&P 500 futures romp higher, close strong.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec S&P 500 futures romp higher, close strong.

text.p: U.S. December Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures romped upward during a spurt of busy afternoon trading to finish with good-sized gains and close at another new all-time high.
Traders cited a litany of factors behind the revived rally, which rescued the index from a soggy morning when futures frequently visited the minus column.

The rash of strong corporate earnings, despite a couple of big exceptions, continued to underpin the cash market. Brokers also pointed to the day's strength in U.S. Treasury bond futures, which only whittled down their gains near the close.

A partial recovery in over-the-counter stocks, which had eased during the morning, plus effects of the expirations of October individual equity options and the October S&P 100 (OEX) index option, also were seen adding lift to a market that many still viewed as leaning strongly higher.
The New York Stock Exchange reported preclosing order imbalances that, just like the morning's preopening imbalances, were sizable and nearly 100 percent buy-side.
Floor brokers also noted talk that a huge stock mutual fund was sighted buying cash shares on Friday.
"There's probably some expiration-related stuff," said one floor analyst. "I heard there was some heavy fund buying today."
"It was busy (with) a lot of shares on the buy-side," said another floor broker.
Others said the market has been caught in an upward draft that even those skeptical about its continued upside potential are leery of flying against.
"The bond market weakened late, and we rallied," added a third broker, who said technicals also continued to bolster futures. "This market's just been strong. It's got momentum."
Although NYSE volume was very heavy, traders said volume was estimated at only about 66,000 in December S&P 500s, which hit and closed just below a record high price of 716.00.

Fair value in December S&P 500s on Friday was about 4.15 points premium, based on the London Interbank Offered Rate. Traders said they saw some signs of arbitrage buy programs, which needed about 4.80 points premium. Arb sell programs would have required about 3.15 points over cash or less.

Dec S&P 500s rose 4.85 to settle at 715.85, Midcap 400s rose 0.40 to 247.65, Value Lines gained 1.55 to 653.60, NYSE Composite up 2.50 at 380.85, Nikkei gained 240.0 to 21,775.0. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
